newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa weaker after seasawing session.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa weaker after seasawing session.

text.p: Cocoa futures ended easier in London on Thursday as short covering dried up after a brief blip to 943 stg per tonne basis May.
The session flip-flopped between lack of buyers and spells of short-covering, leaving traders puzzled about the market's direction after a 80-stg surge since last week.
The board was mixed at the close, but the benchmark May, a highlight of the rally, ended four stg lower on the day at 929 stg a tonne after an early slide to 925 stg.
"I can't say if it was origin-induced or locals had too much cocoa," said one trader.
But switches remained tight, with May/Dec trading at 26 stg from 31 and Sept/Dec at 4-5 stg value.
Turnover totalled a relatively modest 6,051 lots, mainly on May/Dec switches.
"May, July and Sept are on the same boat. If you want to put shorts on the board Dec is the safest bet," said the trader.
The market got off to a weak start but was quickly injected with a dose of short covering which pushed prices to near Wednesday's peak of 945 stg.
But the technical analysts gave a cautious note saying May would have trouble getting through 940 because of oversold chart indicators.
Some players are likely to take May's close below the resistance of 938 as discouraging.
